lessons.explanation:
Echo Bat · Level 2 · Active ally

Retain a measured open-before record, physically replace the section and obtain a fresh intact-after reading. Explain why a powered repeater alone cannot bridge the unchanged break before inviting Echo Bat.

After recruitment, compare the unchanged open case with the restored continuity record. The new view separates receive-and-repeat behavior from repairing the medium; it grants no unreviewed regenerative route.

A repeater regenerates a signal over a connected path. It cannot bridge the severed required conductor. Latest actual bench reading (stale; comparison only): Compatible path: 1 count; Total channel length: 95 m; Inclusive maximum: 100 m; Open required conductors: 0 count; Historical open recorded: 1 count; Repeater role distinguished: 1 count.

Rest Echo Bat

Copperhead Snake · Level 2 · Active ally

At the Warrens and Cavern, retain the actual open-before reading, replace the diagnosed section, then obtain the intact-after reading before inviting Copperhead.

After recruitment, review a fresh remaining-open or overlength example with Copperhead. The new view names the unsatisfied conductor or length check; it cannot repair it.

Continuity and the complete channel length are separate requirements; restoring a conductor does not waive the length bound. Photon the Firefly · Level 2 · Active ally

At the Gardens, inspect the connection and all supplied compatibility fields before applying an intervention. Ask Photon to join after reviewing that demonstration.

After recruitment, ask Photon to compare the five fields of a supplied mismatch with the recorded matching pair. The new view identifies the failed field without changing it.

Current supplied compatibility fields: Fiber/media: matches; Wavelength direction: matches; Supported rate: matches; Connector/polarity: matches; Host support: matches. These independent fields come before optical arithmetic. Inspect, intervene and recheck at the dock; this explanation does not certify a current repair.

Rest Photon the Firefly
Optical inspection and compatible connection checklist: Read and keep all five supplied compatibility checks

SFP Hermit Crab · Level 2 · Active ally

At the Gardens, compare host support, medium, wavelength direction, rate and connector/polarity using the supplied optical pair. Review that accepted demonstration with Hermit Crab at the Vault or Shell Market before inviting it.

After recruitment, compare an actual supplied optical mismatch with the recorded compatible pair. The new view names the unmet profile field; a matching shell or adequate power budget cannot waive it.

Current supplied compatibility fields: Fiber/media: matches; Wavelength direction: matches; Supported rate: matches; Connector/polarity: matches; Host support: matches. These independent fields come before optical arithmetic. Inspect, intervene and recheck at the dock; this explanation does not certify a current repair.

Single-Mode Unicorn · Level 2 · Active ally

Inspect the supplied compatible pair and compare its fresh received power and reserve at the Vault. Return to the Unicorn to review the demonstration and invite it.

After recruitment, use the same declared profile to compare the sensitivity, maximum receive bound and reserve. The new view keeps all three checks distinct, including exact boundaries.

Read sensitivity, maximum receive and required reserve separately. Enough power alone is not proof that every receiver bound is met. Multimode Hydra · Level 2 · Active ally

Inspect a supplied compatible pair and compare its fresh received power and reserve. The Hydra can review either accepted passive path; its identity does not silently change the generic toy profile to multimode.

After recruitment, review the mode explanation beside the same optical result. The new view distinguishes propagation modes from guaranteed payload channels and leaves every physical result unchanged.

Multiple propagation modes do not create guaranteed independent payload lanes. This lesson uses the declared optical profile without inventing a multimode rate or reach bonus. Thunderbird · Level 2 · Active ally

Record compatible settings and the viable path, then measure signal and noise separately. Review the fresh sample with Thunderbird before inviting it.

After recruitment, obtain a later sample and compare it with the earlier attributed reading. The new view labels which is current and explains the changed SNR without inferring throughput or weather causation.

Compare signal and noise in the same measurement. A clear survey does not preserve a link after noise or configuration changes. Electric Eel · Level 2 · Active ally

Sum the declared endpoint demands and compare them with the delivered budget. Review the actual result with Eel before inviting it; the optional Energy Audit is not required.

After recruitment, compare the original over-budget proposal and an accepted kit at the same delivered boundary. The new view shows headroom or excess and keeps per-port and power-method checks separate.

Add simultaneous delivered demand before comparing it with the delivered budget. A per-port capability does not waive that shared total. Chameleon · Level 2 · Active ally

Read both endpoint lists, identify their common 100/full member and inspect the current capability result. Invite Chameleon after explaining why the absent 1000/full choice is unsupported.

After recruitment, compare an unsupported candidate and the reviewed empty-intersection boundary. The new view explains the missing shared mode without inventing a fallback.

A selectable mode must belong to both advertised sets. Faster unilateral selection is not a common mode; an empty intersection cannot negotiate a link.
